what: Certified general-election results for PA-07, one row per major-party nominee. These are historical facts and do not change; the file is committed rather than re-fetched. Finance figures for these candidates are pulled live by collect_fec.py.

notes: DISTRICT BOUNDARIES CHANGED INSIDE THIS WINDOW. 2018 and 2020 were run on the 2018 PA Supreme Court remap; 2022 and 2024 on the post-2020-census remap, which added Carbon County and changed the Monroe County portion. The seat is Lehigh Valley-based throughout, so the four elections are broadly comparable, but they are not the identical electorate.

Susan Wild's FEC candidate record is filed under district 15 for cycle 2018 (candidate_id H8PA15195-era numbering, H8PA15229), because she first filed in the pre-remap PA-15. A query of /elections/?district=07&cycle=2018 therefore OMITS her entirely. Her totals here were pulled directly by candidate_id.

In 2018 Wild simultaneously contested the FULL TERM in the new PA-07 and the UNEXPIRED TERM special election in the old PA-15 (both on 2018-11-06). Her single committee funded both, so her 2018 receipts are not a clean 'PA-07 general election' figure. The vote total used here is the FULL TERM (new PA-07) race.

'Other votes' are third-party and scattered write-in votes reported in the official results. 2018 included a Libertarian (Tim Silfies) who took 3.0% of the vote; the other three cycles were effectively two-candidate races.

Two-party vote share (used for the correlation and regression) is a candidate's votes divided by the sum of the Democratic and Republican votes only. This is the standard comparable measure when third-party presence varies across years, as it does here.

The Clerk of the House summary for 2024 lists only the two major-party nominees and reports no all-candidate district total. Third-party and write-in votes for 2024 are therefore unknown and recorded as null, not zero.
